name: Joppa
overview: Joppa is portrayed in Scripture as a significant seaport, serving as a hub for both trade and travel; for example, cedar trees were brought from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa for export (Ezra 3:7), and Jonah embarked on a ship from Joppa to flee from the Lord’s presence (Jonah 1:3). It was also a place where the early church witnessed God's power, as seen in the story of Tabitha (Dorcas), a disciple known for her good works, whom Peter raised from the dead (Acts 9:36-38). Additionally, Joppa is the setting for Peter’s vision of a sheet lowered from heaven, marking a pivotal moment in the expansion of the gospel to Gentiles.
